title: Engineering Operation Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.
NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.


Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
- Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:
- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of electrical facilities maintenance, or 1+ years of mechanical facilities maintenance experience
- 1+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
- Associate's degree in related field, or technical degree in related field

title: Solutions Architect, Worldwide Public Sector, NPO Charities
descriptionHtml:
Our Mission

We are the trusted advisors and thought leaders who enable Nonprofits to succeed in their missions. We earn trust by listening to our customers, prioritizing their needs, and delivering value so they can make well-informed decisions and create a better world.

About the Role

AWS is looking for a highly motivated Solutions Architect to join the World Wide Public Sector Nonprofits practice. You'll serve as the technical lead for a portfolio of enterprise charities organizations, helping them design and implement cloud architectures.

This role sits within a sales and business development team — your technical expertise will directly inform planning and strategy. You'll need both the consultative and leadership skills to launch projects on a trajectory to success, and the ability to help diverse groups understand application architectures and integration approaches.

What We're Looking For

Someone who is passionate about helping nonprofits achieve their missions through technology. You bring:

- Consultative skills — the ability to listen, understand customer needs, and translate them into technical solutions
- Technical leadership — comfort guiding architectural design decisions and deep-diving into implementation details
- Intellectual curiosity — a drive to keep your technical skills current while maintaining a pulse on industry trends
- Communication skills — experience presenting to small and large groups, from whiteboard sessions to executive briefings
- Operational awareness — understanding of web site/services operations, management, and security

Key job responsibilities

- Own the technical engagement and success of customer implementation projects
- Design cloud architectures leveraging AWS services
- Provide thought leadership on security best practices for applications, servers, and networks
- Respond to RFPs and define implementation approaches
- Serve as a subject matter expert on security as it relates to customer applications and services
- Lead whiteboard sessions, technical deep-dives, and presentations for audiences of all sizes
- Capture and share best practices across the SA community
- Collaborate with and learn from some of the brightest technical minds in enterprise architecture
- Mentor peers and customers while staying current on AWS innovations and industry trends
- Travel up to 30%

A day in the life
You'll provide architectural and technical leadership to nonprofit customers leveraging AWS at scale. You'll guide design decisions with customer obsession, ensuring high availability and performance. You'll evangelize best practices, mentor others, and continuously grow your own expertise.

About the team
We are a dedicated team of Solutions Architects working with nonprofit charities organizations to amplify their mission outcomes.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is seeking exceptional talent to help develop the next generation of advanced robotics systems that will transform automation at Amazon's scale. We're building revolutionary robotic systems that combine cutting-edge AI, sophisticated control systems, and advanced mechanical design to create adaptable automation solutions capable of working safely alongside humans in dynamic environments. This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of robotics and automation at an unprecedented scale, working with world-class teams pushing the boundaries of what's possible in robotic manipulation, locomotion, and human-robot interaction.

We're looking for a Senior Mechanical Engineer to lead mechanical design for advanced manufacturing facilities infrastructure. This role drives the development of new production facilities, delivering scale and efficiency in manufacturing. If you thrive in dynamic environments and enjoy solving complex challenges, this is your opportunity to help shape the future of advanced manufacturing.

title: EMEA Payroll Compliance Manager, Global Payroll Compliance
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is looking for an experienced Payroll Compliance Manager to join our EMEA Payroll Compliance team. In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring payroll compliance across multiple European countries, with a primary focus on France, Spain, Italy, and Germany. You will proactively identify and mitigate payroll compliance risks, and lead responses to regulatory inspections and audits. You will also work with Payroll Tech stakeholders to build scalable process improvements and transformation mechanisms that raise the compliance bar and protect Amazon's employees and the business.

This role offers a unique blend of regulatory depth, cross-border complexity, and technology-driven innovation — ideal for someone who thrives on solving complex compliance challenges at scale. This is a high-impact role that sits at the intersection of payroll operations, human resource, benefits and employment tax and legal. You will work across countries, and across functions to ensure that every employee is paid accurately and in full compliance with local laws.


Key job responsibilities
• Proactively monitor payroll compliance and regulatory updates at a regional level, communicate their impact on business and payroll operations and update policies accordingly.
• Lead proactive compliance assessments across EMEA payroll operations, identifying risks in Social Security contributions, tax withholding, and statutory reporting before they become regulatory findings.
• Design and implement EMEA-wide payroll compliance assessment frameworks with country-specific depth and regional consistency.
• Manage responses to labor inspections, Social Security audits, and tax authority inquiries, coordinating with Legal, Payroll Operations, and external advisors.
• Monitor legislative changes, court rulings, and regulatory guidance across assigned markets and translate them into country-specific operational guidance, process updates, system and control improvements — ensuring payroll calculation accuracy and compliance with applicable laws, policies, and collective bargaining agreements.
• Partner with payroll vendors to validate system configurations, establish compliance checkpoints, and drive remediation of identified gaps.
• Work with Product and Tech teams for automation initiatives and implement compliance control mechanisms that work across countries, legal entities, and payroll platforms
• Partner with HR, Benefits, Legal, Employment Tax, Payroll Technology, and Product teams to develop and enhance existing payroll systems to meet payroll compliance requirements.
• Produce clear, concise compliance risk assessments and present findings and recommendations to senior leadership.


A day in the life
Your primary focus will be ensuring payroll compliance across Western European countries, developing payroll risk control frameworks, payroll blueprints, and compliance rulebooks for mitigating risks, while assisting colleagues across the wider EMEA region. You will respond to stakeholders and/or employee requests on compliance questions, partner with tech colleagues to build AI solutions for risk assessments, and ensure payroll accuracy and compliance. You will join Payroll Product design PODs, where you share compliance requirements, develop self-service mechanisms using AI agents for compliance monitoring, bring new ideas, and learn new opportunities to improve payroll processes and controls.

About the team
The Global Payroll Compliance team within Amazon Finance Operations (FinOps) is a fast-paced, team-focused, dynamic environment. Our mission is to pay employees accurately and on time, every time, with highest controllership and compliance with all regulatory requirements.
You will have opportunities to expand your technical depth, explore new technologies, and contribute ideas that shape the direction of our payroll platform. If you are looking for a team where your work is visible and your development is a priority, this is the place for you.

title: Construction Safety Manager (CSM), DCPD Health and Safety
descriptionHtml:
Do you enjoy taking an idea and turning it into something? Do you ever find yourself marveling at buildings, infrastructure, or landmarks and ask "what does it take to build something like that?" The Construction Safety Manager role is for an experienced Health and Safety (H&S) Specialist, H&S Engineer, or H&S Manager who will support AWS Data Center Planning and Delivery (DCPD) programs. Internally, you will partner with DCPD teams such as Real Estate, Due Diligence, Permitting, Energy, Water, Pre-Construction, Construction, Commissioning, Security and Procurement Teams to achieve health and safety goals and improve our safety culture. Externally, you will engage with General Contractors and AWS Suppliers to confirm/clarify the business expectations for H&S, and look for ways to continually improve H&S of our contracted services. You will work under the direction of the AMER Regional Health & Safety Manager.

Key job responsibilities
This is a field based role, required to report to work at field construction projects in Texas five days per week. Occasional travel to other domestic locations may be required.

You will influence program development, framework, and strategy while deploying programs in the field. This role encompasses implementing health and safety programs across leadership, planning, support, operational controls, continuous improvement, and performance management. You will ensure construction activities meet jurisdictional requirements and AWS Safety Management Program (SMP) standards through systematic compliance and assurance activities.

Examples:
• Review due diligence risk assessments with real estate, pre-construction, construction operations on H&S aspects of the AWS H&S management program to ensure adequate implementation.
• Coordinates with DCPD managers to prioritize H&S in planning and execution in all phases of DCPD projects.
• Ensures & Monitors General Contractors and AWS deployment vendors compliance to onboarding requirements in Avetta.
• Performs campus H&S kickoff sessions, and performs reviews of General Contractor and AWS deployment vendor’s Construction Safety Management Plans
• Documents data and anecdotes in standard reporting tools (Weekly Business Reviews, Monthly Project Reviews) for DCPD and H&S leadership teams
• Manages 3rd party/internal H&S resources on DCPD projects (weekly business reviews, monthly project reviews)
• Identifies improvement opportunities at project(s), and partners with Data Center Health and Safety (DCHS) Operational Team on regional issues that impact construction/operations handover phases.
• Audits projects to the mental model ‘do you have a process, and are you following it?’ Then analyzes data (leading and lagging indicators) for trends, risks/opportunities and reports out at project/regional levels and within governance programs
• Conduct regular site visits with H&S Consultants, construction managers and Data Center Health and Safety Operational teams
• Hosts project and regional specific contractor and internal team H&S kickoff sessions and annual performance review sessions.

A day in the life
This is a field based role, required to report to work at field construction projects in Texas, five days per week. Occasional travel to other domestic locations may be required. This is a unique role that for the right candidate has the potential to take ownership over the entire lifecycle of a Data Center. Starting as a Construction Safety Manager with DCPD on Construction Projects supporting Construction Managers and then transferring safety teams after construction to DCHS as a Regional Safety Manager for the very same buildings in support of Operational Leaders throughout the live space.

You will be integrated with a global network of H&S professionals including Program Managers, other Construction Safety Managers, and Construction Managers. Later in the lifecycle, there is the potential to partner with Operational leaders such as Cluster and Facility Managers, Security Teams, Environmental Partners, as well as other Health & Safety Managers.

You will use data and anecdotes to tactically drive internal customers to manage H&S risks, which includes being an escalation path for issue resolution and managing site-based H&S team members and/or consultants. You will apply your knowledge of the jurisdictional requirements, regional best practices, cultural norms, and location specific characteristics to improve DCPD activities in H&S by jumping in and showing the business “this is what the data is telling us, and this is what actions we should take” and develop DCPD competencies to enable them ownership of your solutions.

You must be an effective communicator, sending clear, concise and consistent messages verbally, in written form, and/or public speaking forums. You will play a key role in deploying mechanisms that manage H&S, while developing competencies and ownership of H&S in the business. You must have diplomacy, patience and tact to earn trust in relationships to effectively advise, instruct and challenge DCPD teams on H&S.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

- 5+ years of compliance, audit or risk management experience
- 8+ years of construction health & safety experience on active construction projects.
- 4+ Years Experience Leading EHS Programs on Construction Projects
- Construction Health & Safety Technician (CHST) Certification

Preferred qualifications

title: Senior Solutions Architect, AWS Industry Automotive and Manufacturing
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon Web Services (AWS), we're looking for a Senior Solutions Architect to join the Automotive & Manufacturing organization within AWS Industries. In this role, you'll shape and lead our technology strategy for global automotive and manufacturing customers and partners, acting as a trusted strategic advisor to some of the largest automotive and manufacturing enterprises in the world. You'll drive the creation of long-horizon technology strategies that tackle complex, often ambiguous business challenges—showing customers how cloud adoption can fundamentally reshape their business outcomes and competitive standing.

As a Senior Solutions Architect, you'll serve as both a technical authority and a strategic influencer—bridging technology vision with measurable, long-term business value for automotive and manufacturing organizations. You'll bring deep technical expertise, executive-level business acumen, and the ability to influence technology strategy at the highest levels, engaging C-suite leaders, business decision makers, and senior technical executives to steer the direction of enterprise-scale cloud transformations.

You'll architect solutions to the most complex challenges—breaking down intricate, multi-system problems into elegant, scalable designs that become reference architectures for the broader SA community. You'll pioneer new architectural patterns and industry-specific methodologies (spanning Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Generative AI, data platforms, and regulated workloads), and you'll shape the product roadmaps of AWS service teams by translating deep customer insight into clear engineering requirements. Working closely with account management, professional services, support, product teams, and the AWS partner ecosystem, you'll own the strategy for driving broad, lasting AWS adoption across your most strategic automotive and manufacturing enterprise customers.

Key job responsibilities
This role powers the success of AWS's most complex and strategic Automotive & Manufacturing engagements. As a Senior Solutions Architect, you'll own solution programs end to end—from strategy to architecture to customer realization—driving measurable, lasting business impact. You'll operate with full autonomy, applying high judgment to decide where to invest your efforts for the greatest organizational and customer value.

A central part of the role is setting the technical and strategic direction for large-scale transformations—including AI/ML and Generative AI programs, data modernization, and regulated cloud migrations. You'll create reusable reference architectures, methodologies, and thought leadership—whitepapers, frameworks, and prescriptive guidance—that scale your impact across the SA community and the wider automotive and manufacturing market.

You'll act as a strategic advisor to your customers' senior leadership, earning trust at the executive level and shaping their long-term technology and business strategy. You'll anticipate emerging customer needs before they're fully articulated, ask the questions customers haven't thought to ask themselves, and lead the consensus-building required to align large, complex organizations around a clear path forward.

A day in the life
Mornings start deep in autonomy workloads—reviewing sensor-fusion pipelines and simulation-at-scale architectures with Motional's perception teams. Midday shifts to Boston Dynamics: whiteboarding fleet telemetry ingestion, edge-to-cloud robotics data flows, and ML training infrastructure for locomotion models. Afternoons mean customer EBCs, unblocking a stuck Kubernetes migration, and pressure-testing cost-optimization strategies. Between meetings, you prototype a reference architecture, mentor account SAs, and align with sales on a multi-year commitment. You close the day translating cutting-edge robotics ambitions into resilient, secure AWS designs—always one step ahead of what autonomous machines will demand next.

Basic qualifications

- 8+ years of specific technology domain areas (e.g. software development, cloud computing, systems engineering, infrastructure, security, networking, data & analytics) experience
- 3+ years of design, implementation, or consulting in applications and infrastructures experience
- 10+ years of IT development or implementation/consulting in the software or Internet industries experience

title: Logistics Program Mgr., AWS Cloud Logistics
descriptionHtml:
As a Transportation Operations Manager, you will serve as the connective tissue between operations execution and performance measurement across both logistics and warehousing services. You will own the full metrics lifecycle — from establishing goals and targets, to tracking performance, to reporting actuals vs. targets for stakeholders across the network. You will simultaneously drive day-to-day operations execution while identifying and implementing structural efficiency improvements that reduce cost, improve throughput, and elevate service levels.

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES:

Metrics Framework & Goal Setting

Design and own the performance metrics framework for transportation and warehousing operations, establishing baseline targets, stretch goals, and tolerance thresholds across key indicators including on-time delivery, warehouse utilization, and carrier performance
Partner with Operations teams and senior leadership to align metrics targets with organizational objectives and network strategy goals
Build and maintain a unified scorecard spanning both logistics (carrier, lane, mode) and warehousing (throughput, labor, space utilization) dimensions, ensuring end-to-end supply chain visibility
Reporting & Actuals vs. Targets Tracking

Develop and publish recurring performance reports — daily, weekly, and monthly — tracking actuals against established targets and surfacing variance trends requiring intervention
Build automated reporting pipelines and dashboards that translate raw operational data into clear, actionable insights for operations managers and senior leadership
Own root cause analysis for metric deviations, documenting findings and driving corrective action plans with accountable stakeholders
Support QBR and MBR reporting cycles with structured narratives that contextualize performance trends against operational and market conditions
Operations Execution

Lead day-to-day transportation and warehousing operations execution, ensuring service continuity, compliance with SOPs, and alignment with carrier and LSP commitments
Serve as an escalation point for operational issues — carrier failures, capacity shortfalls, warehouse throughput bottlenecks — coordinating rapid resolution across internal teams and 3P providers
Operational Efficiency & Continuous Improvement

Identify inefficiencies across transportation lanes and warehousing operations through data analysis, and develop structured improvement initiatives with measurable outcomes
Build and maintain a continuous improvement pipeline — tracking initiative status, projected savings, and realized impact against plan
Develop supplier and carrier performance measurement frameworks that drive accountability and continuous improvement
Partner with category, procurement, and systems teams to align operational efficiency initiatives with broader network strategy and cost reduction goals
Stakeholder Alignment & Cross-functional Partnership

Align with building leadership, regional operations, Finance, and centralized procurement to ensure metrics and efficiency programs reflect both site-level realities and network-wide priorities
Develop relationships across the operations network to ensure best practices in reporting, tracking, and performance management are shared and implemented consistently


A day in the life
The day kicks off reviewing overnight carrier performance dashboards — two lanes missed on-time targets, triggering a root cause deep dive before 8am. By mid-morning, you're in a standup with LSP partners, working through a warehouse throughput bottleneck flagged in yesterday's actuals-vs-targets report. Lunch is spent refining an automated reporting pipeline ahead of next week's MBR. The afternoon brings a cross-functional call with systems and regional ops to align on Q3 efficiency targets. Before signing off, you're updating the continuous improvement tracker — one initiative just hit its projected performance milestone.

- 5+ years of data analysis using tools such as Excel, Pivot Tables, SQL, Tableau, or equivalent experience

title: Senior Financial Analyst, Global Procurement Finance
descriptionHtml:
Have you ever ordered something on Amazon and, when the box arrived, wondered how it got to you so fast, where it came from, and what it cost Amazon to deliver it? We are passionate about numbers and about turning them into insight that moves the business. We are the trusted business advisors who bring the holistic financial perspective to procurement and operations leaders.

You should be excited to join a company that is constantly re-imagining the logistics industry, passionate about using data to solve big, ambiguous problems, eager to keep learning, and attentive to the details that make the difference. title: Security Engineer III, AWS Proactive Security Team
descriptionHtml:
Are you passionate about protecting systems and customers at massive scale? As a Security Engineer III at Amazon, you will lead security risk reduction efforts across teams, tackling complex and ambiguous security challenges that directly safeguard the services millions of customers depend on. In this role, you will design and validate security controls, conduct in-depth security reviews, and build pragmatic solutions that generalize across systems — reducing cost and effort for engineering teams while raising the security bar. You will work at the intersection of technology strategy and risk management, balancing competing constraints to deliver outcomes that are extensible, efficient, and low-friction for builders. If you are a collaborative problem solver who thrives on turning undefined security challenges into repeatable frameworks, we want to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead complex security reviews, threat modeling exercises, and security investigations across your team and partner teams, identifying risks and driving pragmatic mitigation strategies that reduce overall security exposure.
- Design and build security frameworks, runbooks, and rubrics for new problem domains, enabling other engineers to apply your work in a repeatable and scalable way across the organization.
- Engage proactively with product and system owners to review architectures, validate security controls, and guide teams through secure design decisions — including reviewing or writing code, scripts, and detections.
- Communicate security risk and design decisions clearly in writing for both technical and non-technical audiences, and lead inclusive discussions to build consensus when navigating conflicting priorities or trade-offs.
- Mentor and coach multiple security engineers, contribute to hiring assessments, and help establish mature security practices including alarms, telemetry, runbooks, and retrospective processes for your team.

A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing a security design proposal from a partner team, identifying gaps in authentication or data handling and providing actionable feedback. Later, you could lead a threat modeling session for a new service launch, working through risk trade-offs with engineers and stakeholders. In the afternoon, you may write a detection script, update a security runbook, or mentor a teammate on secure coding practices. Throughout it all, you are balancing hands-on technical work with strategic thinking to keep security moving forward.

About the team
Our team is focused on reducing security risk and enabling builders across Amazon to ship securely and confidently. We partner closely with engineering teams to design controls, respond to emerging threats, and raise the overall security posture of the systems we support. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a willingness to challenge assumptions in pursuit of better outcomes. If you are excited about solving hard security problems alongside a talented group of engineers who care deeply about protecting customers, this is the team for you.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture
In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic qualifications

title: Stagiaire Partenaire Ressources Humaines Opérations (6 Mois) - 2027
descriptionHtml:
Résumé du poste

L’énergie qui fait tourner le monde | Découvrez les carrières dans les Opérations

Les postes dans les Opérations chez Amazon vous placent au cœur de la façon dont les choses circulent, d’un simple clic jusqu’à la porte du client.
Vous contribuerez à concevoir, améliorer et faire fonctionner des systèmes qui relient les personnes, les produits et les lieux, à grande échelle. Vous prendrez des responsabilités dès le début, travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes pour résoudre des défis concrets, et verrez les résultats directs de vos décisions lorsqu’elles atteignent les clients chaque jour.
Ici, l’impact de ce que vous construisez n’est pas abstrait : il est visible, immédiat et significatif — il maintient en mouvement l’une des opérations les plus complexes au monde.
C’est ici que votre parcours prend forme, à travers l’action, la responsabilité et la possibilité d’évoluer dans de multiples directions.


Key job responsibilities
Principales responsabilités du poste

- Développer une connaissance approfondie des fonctions RH au sein des opérations dynamiques d’Amazon
- Participer aux efforts de communication interne afin d’aligner les équipes de plusieurs pays, en favorisant la collaboration et le partage d’informations
- Aider à élaborer des plans et des supports de formation répondant aux besoins de développement évolutifs des différentes équipes, afin de soutenir la croissance des collaborateurs et collaboratrices
- Découvrir les fonctions RH au sein de l’organisation Amazon au sens large et se tenir informé(e) des meilleures pratiques
- Apporter un soutien aux employé(e)s d’Amazon sur diverses questions quotidiennes liées à la présence, à l’engagement, à la rémunération et à d’autres sujets RH
- Assister les équipes RH dans les routines opérationnelles quotidiennes et les tâches administratives
- Participer à des revues de processus afin d’identifier des opportunités de simplification et d’automatisation, en améliorant l’efficacité
- Compiler des statistiques du personnel, des rapports et des évaluations de performance complets afin d’éclairer la prise de décision
- Collaborer étroitement avec les responsables opérationnel(le)s afin d’aligner les stratégies et initiatives RH sur les objectifs et priorités de l’organisation


A day in the life
Une journée type

Chaque journée est un peu différente en tant que Stagiaire Partenaire Ressources Humaines Opérations. Ce stage vous plongera dans les RH au sein d’une organisation mondiale, avec la possibilité de travailler sur des projets couvrant différents domaines RH — des relations sociales et de la formation à la rémunération et à l’analyse des effectifs. Vous pourriez passer votre matinée à analyser des données sur les effectifs afin d’identifier des tendances et de formuler des recommandations pour votre équipe, puis votre après-midi à accompagner un dossier de relations sociales ou à collaborer avec des responsables opérationnel(le)s sur une initiative de formation.
La fonction RH d’Amazon est profondément intégrée à l’activité ; ainsi, quel que soit le projet sur lequel vous travaillez, une partie de votre rôle consistera à utiliser les données et la réflexion analytique pour orienter les décisions. Vous appliquerez vos compétences en résolution de problèmes et vos compétences techniques à des défis concrets, tout en développant d’importantes compétences en communication et des compétences comportementales professionnelles grâce à une expérience pratique. Avec un(e) mentor(e) dédié(e) qui accompagnera votre développement tout au long du programme, vous découvrirez comment les RH s’associent à l’activité pour stimuler la croissance et l’excellence organisationnelle — offrant une base solide pour une carrière dans les ressources humaines.
Remarque : vous devez avoir le droit de travailler dans le pays d’emploi à la date de début.


About the team
À propos de l’équipe

Communauté des stagiaires :
En tant que stagiaire Amazon, vous ferez partie d’une communauté dynamique et bienveillante qui favorise votre croissance et votre développement. Vous collaborerez avec des stagiaires du monde entier, développerez votre réseau et participerez à des événements sociaux pour élargir vos perspectives. Vous pourrez également rejoindre des groupes spécialisés axés sur des thèmes tels que la durabilité, afin d’explorer vos centres d’intérêt variés.

Accompagnement :
Le programme de stage offre un solide dispositif d’accompagnement, comprenant des permanences hebdomadaires pour les stagiaires, un support informatique et RH dédié, ainsi qu’une équipe programme engagée dans votre réussite. Cela vous garantit l’encadrement et l’aide nécessaires pour vous épanouir.

Sessions d’apprentissage :
Des sessions d’apprentissage exclusives développeront encore vos compétences, en vous donnant accès aux plateformes d’apprentissage de pointe d’Amazon et à l’expertise de leaders du secteur. Ces opportunités de développement structurées vous prépareront à l’étape suivante de votre carrière.

Opportunités :
À l’issue réussie du stage, vous pourrez être considéré(e) pour un poste de jeune diplômé(e) ou un second stage, vous permettant de poursuivre votre parcours avec Amazon. De plus, vous bénéficierez d’un salaire mensuel compétitif, d’un soutien à la relocalisation et d’un accès à une gamme d’avantages réservés aux employés.

Dates de début des stages tout au long de l’année :
Nous recrutons des stagiaires pour un début à tout moment entre janvier et septembre 2027. Chaque mois, nous organiserons 1 à 2 journées d’intégration pour les nouveaux et nouvelles arrivant(e)s.

Basic qualifications

- Actuellement en dernière année et préparant une licence ou un master universitaire en RH, administration des affaires, psychologie, marketing, sciences sociales, droit ou dans un domaine connexe (à orientation sciences humaines), ou dans une discipline similaire
- Disponible pour un stage à temps plein (35 heures/semaine) et s'engager sur un stage de 6 mois
- Parler, écrire et lire couramment l'anglais et le français à un niveau C1 ou supérieur
- Obligatoire de pouvoir signer une convention de stage avec l'université de l'étudiant(e)

Preferred qualifications

- Solides compétences en résolution de problèmes et en analyse, avec la capacité d'utiliser les données pour orienter les décisions
- Excellentes compétences en communication et en travail d'équipe, avec la capacité de collaborer efficacement avec diverses parties prenantes
- Curiosité, proactivité et volonté avérées d'apprendre et de se développer dans un environnement dynamique

Amazon est un employeur engagé pour l'égalité des chances. Nous sommes convaincus qu'une main d'oeuvre diversifée est essentielle à notre réussite. Nous prenons nos décisions de recrutement en fonction de votre expérience et de vos compétences. Nous apprécions votre envie de découvrir, d'inventer, de simplifier et de construire. title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Platform Engineering & Services
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Fulfillment Technologies (AFT) powers the physical engine at the heart of Amazon. AFT builds and operates software, hardware, and the processes that run the global network of fulfillment centers that move billions of units of inventory, employ tens of thousands of people, and ensure that customers get what they want when promised. We do this by building automated solutions to handle things that technology does well, while relying on people to handle things that humans do well. We use innovative technologies to simplify the process by taking advantage of materials handling automation, mathematical optimization, computer vision, robotics, and machine learning. Our highly scalable distributed systems are designed to handle billions of transactions a year.
The AFT PES is seeking an innovative, intellectually curious, results-oriented technology leader who will be responsible for driving our product roadmap and aligning cross-functionally both in terms of guiding the design/development within our group and getting the work prioritized across multiple teams/stakeholders. You will act as a leader who can set the team vision and tone, articulate clear goals and priorities, and ensure delivery excellence. You are able to handle business escalations with a data-driven approach. This role provides clear, comprehensive and timely status updates, including decisions made, tradeoffs and any escalations needed to remove obstacles to all stakeholders. title: Software Development Engineer II, Enterprise Productivity

You will own the full software development lifecycle — from working backwards to understand customer needs, through design, implementation, testing, deployment, and ongoing operations. title: Data Center Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic AWS team and become a critical guardian of global cloud infrastructure! You'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of the world's most innovative technology platform, ensuring seamless data center operations that power millions of businesses and services worldwide.

Data Center Technicians should be willing to work both independently and with a team. Work prioritization, organizational skills, effective communication, and the ability to react quickly are critical to success. In addition to hardware and network repair, candidates will install equipment, create documentation, innovate solutions, and fix problems within the data center space. This team works in an environment that operates 24/7. Traveling within and outside of the regional work area is required.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: PDX is an AWS GovCloud region. As required by our contracts with the federal government, effective February 24, 2026, logical access to the AWS GovCloud region will be restricted to Amazon employees who are U.S. Citizens. (GovCloud may NOT be accessed from outside of the United States).

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
- Performing server rack installations, hardware break-fix on various components, troubleshooting network issues, responding to operational incidents that impact service availability, and carrying out routine network, server hardware, and operating system repairs to contribute to the overall availability of AWS services

Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

title: Sr. HR Manager
descriptionHtml:
In pursuit of being Earth's Best Employer, our global Human Resources teams, known as People eXperience and Technology (PXT), drive business success by fostering a safe, inclusive, and innovative culture. The Senior PXT Campus Manager is a strategic, high-judgment leader responsible for delivering operational excellence and scalable PXT impact across the most complex sites and regions. Leading a team of HR Partners and HR Business Partners, you will partner with Snr Business and Amazon site Leaders, to translate enterprise people strategies into regional execution, strengthen leadership capability, and drive systemic improvements in culture, performance, and risk. Success requires your ability to flex based on business conditions, surface trends and scale practices regionally, guide PXT site leaders through complex high-impact decisions, anticipate emerging risks, and influence senior stakeholders. You will drive measurable improvements in attrition, attendance, engagement, and leadership effectiveness across multiple sites while building a high-performing, future-ready PXT organization.
You will be expected to travel and work onsite at Amazon facilities, ensuring personal connection and hands-on leadership where needed.


Key job responsibilities
PXT Operational Excellence
Ensure PXT teams across your region execute with discipline, consistency, and alignment to Amazon standards. Use inspections and data to identify defects, validate process integrity, and reinforce accountability. Deep dive executive escalations, ethics cases, and workplace incidents to identify root causes and address systemic issues. Surface recurring system gaps to central teams, influencing scalable improvements. Champion PXT tools and systems while reinforcing critical thinking. Establish consistent inspection rhythms to monitor progress and escalate persistent gaps. Maintain visibility across sites, building rapport and identifying concerns before they escalate.

Employee Experience & Culture
Set clear expectations for site and PXT leaders to create workplace environments that drive engagement, performance, and retention. Ensure leaders implement feedback mechanisms including Voice of the Associate boards, roundtables, and GEMBA walks. Oversee employee relations budgets and deliver meaningful recognition programs. Champion safety-first culture through proactive strategies, inspections, and accountability. Partner with leaders to uphold building standards and empower community engagement initiatives coordinated with Public Policy and Public Relations teams.

PXT Leadership
Guide high-judgment decisions impacting people, performance, and culture. Provide oversight on investigations, corrective actions, and employee relations matters, serving as final decision-maker on high-risk decisions including terminations involving potential discrimination, retaliation, for business leaders. Serve as primary escalation point for complex issues, partnering with Regional PXT, Legal, and Employee Relations teams. Anticipate and mitigate employee relations risks by identifying emerging trends and developing proactive strategies. Partner with country-level Governance teams and Works Council representatives to ensure effective consultation processes on site-level matters, maintaining constructive labor relations and compliance with co-determination requirements. Lead regional change initiatives by supporting site leaders through transformation, helping manage ambiguity and reinforce new behaviors. Foster collaboration between site and central PXT teams. Drive adoption of HR technology solutions to enhance efficiency and employee experience.

Ops Talent Planning & Org Health
Partner with Operations leaders to assess organizational health, review succession plans, and identify gaps in leadership capability or bench strength. Hold PXT teams accountable for building leadership capability through coaching and development. Partner with business leaders to identify leadership gaps and drive targeted development. Review talent strategies, identify risks, and align on regional priorities. Ensure site teams evaluate leadership readiness, role criticality, and attrition trends. Identify critical roles with limited bench strength or high retention risk, developing targeted contingency plans. Drive consistent, objective talent evaluations and ensure performance tools are used to drive fair, defensible outcomes.

PXT Leadership & Org Health
Build and sustain a high-performing, future-ready PXT organization. Invest in PXT team growth through coaching, development, and stretch opportunities. Drive succession and promotion decisions by assessing performance, readiness, and potential. Create meaningful opportunities for PXT site leaders to lead regional initiatives and extend their influence. Set the tone for an inclusive, connected, high-trust culture, using data to assess team health. Ensure regional PXT strategy aligns with broader organizational goals while adapting to local needs. Oversee PXT headcount across the region, ensuring appropriate staffing and resourcing. Translate Amazon PXT priorities into clear, actionable regional plans with defined goals and metrics.


A day in the life
Your day blends strategic leadership with operational execution across multiple complex sites. You'll partner with senior Business and HR Leaders and on high-impact organizational challenges while coaching your team of HR Partners and HR Business Partners. You'll flex based on business conditions, conducting site walks to assess standards and safety, facilitating feedback sessions, and reviewing regional metrics to surface trends. You'll make high-judgment decisions on investigations and corrective actions, manage complex escalations, and lead regional change initiatives. Through data analysis and inspection routines, you'll identify systemic issues and influence central teams on scalable improvements. Success comes from your ability to lead through others, anticipate emerging risks, and drive measurable improvements in employee experience and business performance across your region.

- Extensive experience in human resources leadership or equivalent leadership experience (e.g., operations, customer service, retail, distribution, shipping/logistics, healthcare, hospitality, manufacturing)

- Fluent verbal and written communication skills in English and Spanish

- Experience supporting and/or leading employee-focused processes such as onboarding, benefits, investigations, training and/or talent management

descriptionHtml:

What's in it for you? An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You'll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.

Amazon internships are full-time positions, and interns should expect to work Monday-Friday, up to 40 hours per week typically between 8am-5pm. Specific team norms around working hours will be communicated by your manager. Interns should not have conflicts such as classes or other employment during the Amazon work-day.
Applicants should have a minimum of one quarter/semester/trimester remaining in their studies after their internship concludes.

By applying to this position, your application will be considered for all ASIC roles at all locations we hire for in the United States including but not limited to: Greater Seattle Area (Seattle, Bellevue, Redmond), Greater Bay Area (San Francisco, Sunnyvale, Santa Clara), Greater DMV (DC, MD, VA), Austin (TX), New York City (NY), Minneapolis (MN).

• Develop and execute design automation mechanisms and flows.

You must be responsive, flexible and able to succeed within an open collaborative peer environment.

title: SDE II, EE Experiences, Progressive Discovery and Monetization
descriptionHtml:
Everyday Essentials (EE) is a $100B+ business and one of the fastest-growing categories at Amazon — the household staples, health and personal care, grocery, and beauty products hundreds of millions of customers reorder. We're reinventing how customers discover, buy, and get more value from them, and we're looking for Software Development Engineers who want to build that future.

The EE Experiences organization builds the shopping experience for the products customers come back for most. Our charter is Progressive Discovery and Monetization: helping customers find better products for their needs, complete their baskets, and improve EE business economics — and giving the world's largest consumer brands new and effective ways to reach those customers and grow with Amazon. We build a durable, profitable business at the intersection of the two, on the surfaces customers use every day.

This is a space where the hardest problems don't have off-the-shelf answers. We're not polishing a solved product — we're inventing experiences that don't exist yet, and the decisions we make now shape a business with room to grow for years. You'll build discovery and recommendation features, brand-facing advertising surfaces, and the backend services that power them. Your work moves from whiteboard to production in front of a very large customer base, with visibility all the way to senior leadership.

We're an AI-first team, and that shows up in two ways. We use AI throughout how we build software, and we expect our engineers to keep learning and applying the latest tools to move faster and raise the quality bar. AI is also at the core of what we build — the intelligence that helps customers find the right product is a modeling and engineering problem we work on hand in hand with scientists. If you're curious about AI, learn quickly, and like using it to solve real customer problems while keeping a clear head about where it helps and where it doesn't, you'll fit right in.

Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and own software end to end — from customer research through design, code, testing, deployment, and production operations.
Take on ambiguous problems where the goal is clear but the path is not, bring clarity, and deliver simple solutions that improve how customers find and buy everyday essentials.
Partner closely with scientists, product managers, and designers to turn customer and brand problems into products that ship worldwide.
Use generative AI tools and modern engineering practices to raise quality and velocity, and coach teammates on getting the most from them.
Own operational health for your services — monitor metrics, drive root-cause fixes, and keep improving the experience for customers and brand partners.
Raise the technical bar through code reviews, mentoring, and hiring for the best talent.

A day in the life
Most days start with the customer problem in front of you: how to help someone find better everyday-essentials products faster, or how to give brands a more effective way to reach shoppers or how to improve the profitability of the business. You dig into data, sketch a design, and talk it through with product managers and scientists before writing any code. By the afternoon you might be prototyping an idea that didn't exist yesterday, reviewing a teammate's change, or debugging something in production. Because so much here is new, you won't just pick up tickets. You'll help decide what to build, push for the approach you believe in, and see your work reach customers in weeks, not quarters.

About the team
Our team owns how customers discover and buy the everyday essentials they rely on — and how the brands behind those products reach them. Our mission is to make restocking the things you need effortless, help customers find better options and to improve the business economics along the way. Day to day you'll work with fellow engineers and partner closely with product managers, designers, and scientists, who bring the customer and data insight that shapes what we build. We're a small, fast-moving group solving open-ended problems for hundreds of millions of shoppers — a place where you own problems end to end and your ideas reach customers fast.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Experience building complex software systems that have been successfully delivered to customers
- Experience debugging, profiling, and implementing best software engineering practices in large-scale systems

You will partner with employees as well as contractors to achieve health and safety goals and improve our already strong safety culture. You will work in a fast-paced environment where our operations are rapidly changing, advocating safe changes in the face of new infrastructure, new tools, and new products/processes.

title: Electronics Manufacturing Manager, Amazon Center for Quantum Computing
descriptionHtml:
The Amazon Center for Quantum Computing is seeking a Production Manager to lead the medium-volume production of control electronics systems for our experimental quantum computing platforms. Operating at a scale of hundreds of units per year, you will own the end-to-end production process for chassis-level and board-level electronics assemblies — from intake of engineering designs through assembly, test, and delivery to internal customers. You will manage and develop a small team of assembly and test technicians, setting the quality standards, work instructions, and processes that ensure consistent, reliable output. Beyond production execution, you will own the production laboratory space itself, including inventory management and the physical organization and standards of the facility. You will also co-manage the product lifecycle management (PLM) system alongside adjacent hardware engineering and business teams, ensuring alignment across design, production, and program management. The ideal candidate brings a proven track record in electronics production at similar volumes, a hands-on understanding of what it takes to build and test complex electronic assemblies repeatably, and the leadership skills to build a high-performing production team from the ground up.

Key job responsibilities
- Own end-to-end production of control electronics assemblies (chassis builds, board-level assemblies, cable harnesses) at medium volume, managing the full lifecycle from procurement through assembly, test, and delivery.
- Lead production scheduling and capacity planning, managing trade-offs between product mix, technician utilization, and delivery commitments.
- Manage and develop a team of assembly and test technicians, setting standards, building a culture of quality and accountability, and serving as a technical escalation resource.
- Own the production laboratory space, including equipment, tooling, inventory, and environmental controls; co-manage the PLM system with adjacent hardware engineering and business teams.
- Partner with hardware engineering to provide DFM and DFT feedback on new designs, and lead root cause analysis and corrective action for production defects and quality escapes.
- Manage supply chain relationships, proactively identifying and mitigating component availability risks and lead-time issues.
- Drive continuous improvement through lean principles and process optimization; work with engineering and senior management to develop and execute production roadmaps aligned with the team's scaling plans.

A day in the life
Your morning starts with a technician standup, then a supply chain issue — a connector slipped its delivery date — that you work through with procurement. Mid-morning you walk the floor, inspecting work in progress. After lunch you flag a component placement problem in a new board design before it reaches production. Later you draft a work instruction update for a chassis assembly that keeps generating rework. You close the day in a roadmap review with senior management, presenting capacity forecasts and the infrastructure investments needed to hit next quarter's scaling targets.

About the team
You will join SIGNALS, a multidisciplinary team responsible for all electronics and signal delivery solutions in Amazon's quantum computing systems — spanning from the programmable logic software layer down to microwave signal delivery at the quantum processor package. The team brings together software, electrical, RF, and mechanical engineers solving tightly coupled problems across the full signal chain. As Production Manager, you will be the critical link between engineering design and production reality, ensuring the team's innovations are built reliably and delivered on schedule.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
- 5+ years of experience in electronics production, manufacturing, or test engineering.
- Hands-on experience with chassis-level and board-level electronics assembly processes.
- 2+ years of experience managing or supervising technicians or production staff.
- Working knowledge of inventory management and PLM, MRP, or ERP systems.
- Demonstrated ability to develop and implement production standards, work instructions, and quality processes.

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in engineering, manufacturing, or operations management.
- Experience with medium-volume, high-mix production environments (hundreds to low thousands of units per year).
- Familiarity with IPC standards for electronics assembly and workmanship.
- Experience managing supply chains for custom or low-volume electronic assemblies, including component obsolescence and alternate sourcing.
- Background in scientific instrumentation, aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability electronics production.
- Experience providing DFM and DFT feedback to hardware engineering teams.

descriptionHtml:
This position requires in-role training at an operating site which will be 2+ weeks in duration. This training will be located 50+ miles away from the home site location. All travel accommodations for training will be booked and paid for by Amazon.

Please note: this role requires open flexibility to work 10 hour overnight shifts (late afternoon to early morning hours) and will be scheduled on a front-half (Sunday – Wednesday) or back-half (Wednesday – Saturday) schedule. Shifts will be assigned upon starting in the role and could be subject to change based upon business need.


ABOUT AMAZON

Our Worldwide Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Area Manager. In this role, you will lead a team of hourly employees and will be responsible for engaging your team during their shifts to maintain the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance, and performance. You will also play a key part in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location.

title: Program Manager, EU Ops Sustainability
descriptionHtml:
EU Operations Sustainability drives the decarbonization of Amazon's operational footprint across Europe, focusing on reducing environmental impact from transportation, buildings, and energy consumption. The team develops and executes strategies spanning First Mile, Middle Mile, and Last Mile logistics — including energy efficiency, renewable energy, building material decarbonization and climate resiliency and adaptation, at fulfillment centers, sort centres and delivery stations. Working cross-functionally with EU Operations, WW Sustainability, engineering and procurement, the EU Ops Sustainability team translates Amazon's Climate Pledge commitments into actionable programs with measurable targets. The team navigates also the evolving European regulatory landscape to ensure compliance while identifying opportunities to accelerate decarbonization ahead of mandated timelines.

EU Ops Sustainability is looking for a Sustainability Program Manager to support energy efficiency programs across all miles. In this role, you will own strategic, tactical, and cross-functional projects and programs within the STEP organization to meet sustainability goals. You will be responsible for scoping and creating project plans, developing processes, coordinating and driving execution, and communicating progress to senior leadership. You will work day-to-day with cross-functional partners including RME, Finance, Real Estate, Design & Construction (D&C), and IT to deliver measurable energy and carbon reductions. You will also have the opportunity to work with selected start-ups through the Amazon Sustainability Accelerator (ASA) – Climate Tech programme, helping to evaluate, pilot, and scale innovative sustainability technologies across Amazon's European fulfillment network.

This role can be also based in other EU cities: Paris (CDG10), Barcelona (BCN10), Madrid (MAD12), Milan (LIN15), and Munich (MUC11).

The applicable collective agreement for this role is CBA for employees of Logistics, Delivery and Shipping Sector 
The position is classified at level 1 or above, depending on the candidate's skills, competences and experience.

Key job responsibilities
- Manage full lifecycle complex cross-functional programs with considerable impact across multiple organizations
- Work closely with partner teams and stakeholders in and outside of your organization to source, allocate, and coordinate resources
- Build and own financial models including business cases, Capital Appropriation Request (CAR) submissions, and discounted payback period (DPP) analysis to justify energy efficiency investments;
- Own reporting on the state of initiatives, measuring improvements and impact of changes
- Navigate the evolving European regulatory landscape — including EPBD (Energy Performance of Buildings Directive), Décret Tertiaire, and ISO 50001 to ensure compliance and identify opportunities to accelerate decarbonization ahead of mandated timelines
- Work autonomously in an ambiguous environment, seeking to understand business problems, automation limitations, scaling factors, boundary conditions and reasons behind leadership decisions
- Solve ambiguous problems and proactively identify and mitigate risks (before they become roadblocks)
- Work with program managers, business leaders and executive team to communicate and impact critical business initiatives
- Develop, implement, and govern Key Performance Metrics (KPI) reporting for a portfolio of programs, providing visibility to the milestones, and performance across all projects
- Set-up mechanisms to audit and perform necessary course corrections where needed to meet business objectives

EU STEP brings together Supply Chain, Network Design, and Transportation Planning teams to improve end-to-end forecasting, network flow, planning, and execution. title: Software Development Engineer, Building Connectivity Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Every Amazon data center runs on networks no customer ever sees: the corporate network that engineers and tools use to reach the fleet, the segmented networks that cameras and badge readers ride on, the network for building systems, and the isolated controls networks behind power and cooling. Building Connectivity Engineering (BCE), part of AWS Networking, owns the design and operation of those fabrics in every Amazon data center, and builds them into more than 100 new sites a year. Building Connectivity Software Systems (BCSS) is the software team inside BCE.

We build the controller for these networks. It holds the intended state of every fabric as a model, computes everything a new site needs (addresses, routing identifiers, ports, cabling, device registration) before a technician plugs in the first rack, renders device configuration from the model, and drives the deployment and monitoring platforms that AWS Networking already runs. The first production release went live in September 2026 and took a site build that used to need about twenty hand-run steps down to one request. Most of the controller is still ahead of us.

We are hiring Software Development Engineers to build the next releases: a versioned model of intended network state with full history and rollback, device configuration rendered from that model instead of written by hand, and the orchestration that takes a site from a plan to live traffic with one physical touch. You will design services, write the design documents for them, build them on AWS, prove them in shadow mode against real sites, and run them in production. The network engineers who hold the fabric knowledge are your partners; your code is the engine their models run on.

Key job responsibilities
* Design and build services in AWS (Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB, EventBridge, CDK), modeled with Smithy and deployed through pipelines you own.
* Write the design document for what you build. Every engineer on this team writes designs; it is a core part of the job, and seniority is not the gate.
* Integrate with the systems of record in AWS Networking (IP address management, device registry, routing-policy store, configuration store and release, deployment, cabling plans), and find out what each contract actually does, against the real service, before committing to a date.
* Prove correctness in shadow mode: compute what the automation would do for a site, diff it against what engineers did by hand, and get to zero discrepancies before any cutover.
* Own what you ship in production: metrics, alarms, runbooks, and a turn in the team's on-call rotation, which covers the new services and the ones the team inherited.
* Keep fabric knowledge out of the code. New fabrics, site types and rack types arrive as models the network engineers author; your job is to make the second one cost a configuration change.
* Estimate honestly: size work by how novel it is and how many systems outside the team it touches, raise partner asks early, and say what is unknown.

A day in the life
You pick up a card to add a new reservation type to the allocation service. Before writing code you spend an hour against the real partner API in a test account and find that the contract does not do what its wiki page says, so you write that down, re-size the card, and raise the ask with the partner team that morning instead of three weeks in. The afternoon is a design review of a teammate's state machine change, where the question you keep asking is what happens on the retry, and your own code review landing with its shadow-mode diff attached. A few times a year you are the on-call engineer for a week, and the team expects that week to be your work.

About the team
BCSS, formed in May 2026. We bring software engineering practice to a problem space that has not had software developers, and we never cut corners: slow is smooth, and smooth is fast. Our stance in one line is a team tenet: we don't just make a change, we make a changer. Our software runs on AWS and operates entirely detached from production data traffic.

We work inside an operating model where network fabric teams run like software teams: they own their business logic, expose APIs, and measure outcomes. BCSS builds the software; every fabric team owns its automation roadmap and its adoption. Design reviews are open and argued; the best objection in the room wins, whoever raised it.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
- Experience architecting/operating solutions built on AWS
- Experience owning and leading significant projects from concept to deployment
- Experience working with networking fundamentals or Internet protocols such as TCP/IP, UDP, SSL, DNS, HTTP/S, or equivalent
- Experience with workflow orchestration and event-driven designs (Step Functions, EventBridge or equivalents), including idempotency, retries and rollback
- Experience integrating with systems whose APIs you do not control, and designing for their failure modes
- Experience with data modeling: versioned data, graph-shaped data, or generating configuration or code from a model

descriptionHtml:
Operations is the beating heart of Amazon. This key part of our business makes sure we fulfil and dispatch orders efficiently so that our customers get their items on time. It's driven by Operations Managers who bring the team together to push excellence in safety, quality and productivity across our sites. At your site, you'll lead other managers and create the operational plan that helps your teams meet their targets. This role is all about driving operational excellence to create the Amazon of tomorrow.

Key job responsibilities
- Manage and develop a team of Area Managers
- Lead operational teams on a shift, deal with issues, and positively impact site performance
- Analyse shift performance against relevant business objectives, and put in place actions to improve our operational excellence
- Work closely with other support teams, including HR, Finance, Health and Safety, and Security

A day in the life
You'll lead shifts at one of our operational sites. You'll also be the key link between a number of teams, including finance, safety and operations integration teams. That means you'll be close to the day-to-day operations at your site but also contribute to new ways to innovate at your site.

A typical day will involve meetings with different areas of the business, deep diving into performance and risk metrics for sites, and looking ahead to prepare for different levels of demand. Amazon Logistics, or AMZL, handles 'last mile' delivery duties in partnership with third-party distribution businesses.
